paragraphs.title: The Division of the Land and the Sacred Contribution

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “ye shall offer an oblation unto the Lord, an holy portion of the land.”
easy.q: To whom was the holy portion of the land offered?

easy.explanation: Verse 1 gives the breadth as ten thousand reeds.
easy.q: What was the breadth of the holy portion of the land?

answers: For the whole house of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says the city possession “shall be for the whole house of Israel.”
easy.q: For whom was the possession of the city appointed?

answers: The sanctuary and the most holy place
medium.explanation: Verse 3 says that the sanctuary and the most holy place were in this portion.
medium.q: What was located within the portion measuring twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth?

medium.explanation: The suburbs were the surrounding area set apart around the sanctuary.
medium.q: What does “suburbs” mean in the phrase “fifty cubits round about for the suburbs thereof”?

answers: It gave him a defined possession so he would not oppress the people
It gave him all the land of Israel
medium.explanation: Verse 8 says the princes would no more oppress the people, while the land would be given to Israel according to their tribes.
medium.q: How was the prince’s possession related to protecting the people?

answers: Sanctuary, priestly and Levitical areas, city, and the prince’s possession
The prince’s possession without any sacred areas
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the sanctuary, the priests, the Levites, the city, and the prince’s portions.
challenge.q: What general order of land allocation appears in these verses?

answers: The land division was intended for all Israel, not only its rulers
The priests would receive all the land
The city would replace the tribal inheritances
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 specifically says the rest of the land would be given to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that the land would be given to the house of Israel according to their tribes?

answers: It was on both sides of the holy contribution and the city
It was located inside the sanctuary
It was located only inside the city
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 says there would be a portion for the prince “on the one side and on the other side” of the holy portion and city.
challenge.q: What was distinctive about the location of the prince’s possession?

easy.q: What were the princes of Israel commanded to remove?

answers: Balances, an ephah, and a bath
easy.explanation: Verse 10 names just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.
easy.q: Which measures were to be just?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “the shekel shall be twenty gerahs.”
easy.q: How many gerahs were in a shekel?

answers: Both promote fairness toward the people
medium.explanation: The passage joins righteous government with honest balances and standard measures.
medium.q: What connection is made between justice and accurate commercial measures?

answers: Remove oppressive demands and burdens from the people
medium.explanation: The context calls the princes to remove violence, execute justice, and stop oppressive demands.
medium.q: What does the command to take away the princes’ “exactions” from the people mean?

answers: The ephah was ten times larger than the bath
The bath was ten times larger than the ephah
medium.explanation: Verse 11 says, “The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure.”
medium.q: What relationship did the ephah and the bath have?

answers: Leaders are responsible for protecting the people from oppression
Leaders may use different measures for different people
The people alone are responsible for justice
challenge.explanation: The princes are commanded to remove violence and spoil and to execute judgment and justice.
challenge.q: What principle of leadership is expressed in the command to the princes?

answers: To prevent dishonesty in trade and offerings
challenge.explanation: The use of just balances and fixed measures would prevent unfair dealing.
challenge.q: Why was it important for the measures to have fixed standards?

answers: Standardization was required even for units of weight
Each merchant could establish a different standard
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 specifies the gerahs, shekels, and maneh, showing that weights were to be carefully regulated.
challenge.q: What does the detailed description of the maneh and shekel suggest?

paragraphs.title: The People's Contributions and Public Offerings

easy.explanation: Verses 13–15 mention wheat, barley, oil, and lambs from the flock.
easy.q: What products were included in the people’s contribution?

easy.explanation: Verse 17 says it would be the prince’s part to provide these offerings.
easy.q: Who was responsible for the burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings at the appointed times?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 requires one lamb from the flock out of two hundred.
easy.q: How many lambs were required from every two hundred?

answers: For a meat offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings
medium.explanation: Verse 15 lists the meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings.
medium.q: For what purposes were the lambs given?

answers: A liquid offering accompanying the worship service
medium.explanation: The drink offering is listed with the burnt, meat, and peace offerings as part of worship.
medium.q: What is a “drink offering” in this context?

answers: The people gave the contribution, and the prince provided the offerings at the appointed times
The prince provided everything, and the people gave nothing
The people provided only Temple vessels
medium.explanation: Verse 16 assigns the contribution to the people, while verse 17 assigns the public offerings to the prince.
medium.q: How were the responsibilities divided between the people and the prince?

answers: Public participation was organized according to established measures
Each person gave only according to personal preference
The contributions were required only during wartime
challenge.explanation: The passage gives definite proportions for grain, oil, and sheep.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fixed rates of the contributions?

answers: It shows that his responsibility was public, not merely personal
It exempted the people from every act of worship
It gave him the priests’ inheritance
challenge.explanation: Verse 17 says the prince would prepare the offerings “to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.”
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the prince provided offerings for the house of Israel?

answers: The contribution supplied offerings used to make reconciliation for the people
The contribution was used only to build houses
The contribution had no connection with offerings
challenge.explanation: The grain, oil, and lamb contributions supported the offerings made for reconciliation.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the people’s contribution and reconciliation?

paragraphs.title: Purification and Inauguration of the Temple

easy.explanation: Verse 18 commands the taking of a young bullock without blemish.
easy.q: What offering was taken on the first day of the month?

answers: He put it in specified places in the Temple
He poured it outside the land
He gave it to the prince
easy.explanation: Verse 19 places the blood on the posts of the house, the altar’s corners, and the inner court gate.
easy.q: What did the priest do with the blood of the sin offering?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “And so thou shalt do the seventh day of the month.”
easy.q: On what other day of the month was a similar action performed?

answers: To establish the value of the shekel
medium.explanation: Verse 18 says the bullock was taken to “cleanse the sanctuary.”
medium.q: What was the purpose of the offering on the first day of the month?

answers: The sides or supports of a doorway
A dwelling place for the Levites
medium.explanation: Posts are the upright sides or supports of a doorway.
medium.q: What does “posts” mean in the phrase “the posts of the house”?

answers: For one who erreth and for him that is simple
medium.explanation: Verse 20 mentions “every one that erreth, and for him that is simple.”
medium.q: For whom was reconciliation made on the seventh day?

answers: The rite involved the house, the altar area, and the inner court gate
The blood was applied only outside the Temple
The rite took place only in the priests’ houses
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 names several locations throughout the Temple complex.
challenge.q: What can be learned from applying the blood in several places in the Temple?

answers: Both involved cleansing or reconciliation for the Temple
The first concerned the city and the seventh concerned the prince
Only the first day was connected with the Temple
challenge.explanation: The first day cleansed the sanctuary, and the seventh day provided reconciliation for the house.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the first and seventh days?

answers: It addressed sin committed through error or simplicity
It made no reference to sin
challenge.explanation: Verse 20 specifically includes the person who errs and the person who is simple.
challenge.q: What moral distinction appears in the description of the rite?

paragraphs.title: Passover and the Feast of Booths

easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the passover.”
easy.q: On what day of the month was the Passover observed?

easy.explanation: Verse 21 calls it “a feast of seven days” during which unleavened bread was eaten.
easy.q: How long did the feast of unleavened bread last?

easy.explanation: Verse 23 requires seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily.
easy.q: How many bullocks and rams were offered daily during the seven days of the feast?

answers: A bullock for a sin offering
medium.explanation: Verse 22 says the prince prepared a bullock for a sin offering.
medium.q: What did the prince prepare on Passover for himself and the people?

answers: An offering made from grain or meal
medium.explanation: The meat offering is measured by an ephah and is associated with grain or meal.
medium.q: What does “meat offering” mean in this passage?

answers: Two ephahs for a bullock and ten for a ram
medium.explanation: Verse 24 says, “an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram.”
medium.q: What measure of meat offering was appointed for a bullock and a ram?

answers: The prince provided offerings for the people at both feasts
Both feasts lasted seven days of unleavened bread
challenge.explanation: The prince provided offerings at Passover, and verse 25 says he would do the like at the seventh-month feast.
challenge.q: What similarity appears between Passover and the feast in the seventh month?

answers: The sin offering was a kid of the goats, while the burnt offering included bullocks and rams
The sin offering was a ram, while the burnt offering was a goat
There was no difference between the offerings
challenge.explanation: Verse 23 distinguishes a daily kid of the goats for a sin offering from the bullocks and rams for burnt offerings.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between the sin offering and the burnt offerings at the feast?

answers: The same general arrangement was to be followed for the seven days
Offerings were given only on the first day
The feast lasted only one day
challenge.explanation: Verse 25 says the prince would do the like in the seven-day feast.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of the offering arrangement for the feast in the seventh month indicate?
